findings.title: Inventory PATCH can move a line out of Sold or off a pending transfer, bypassing the PO cascade's status rules
findings.evidence: The only status guard is LINE_STATUSES membership plus 'committed claims > 0' (committedClaimsByLine counts Shipped/Awaiting payment, not Done). The PO cascade refuses the same moves: leaving Sold (orderAdvance.ts:261-263), lines claimed by a Pending transfer (transferClaimedLineIds, orderAdvance.ts:166-169), and lines named by open Draft/Packing sell orders (orderAdvance.ts:205-211).
findings.failure_scenario: (a) A lot sold out by a Done SO keeps its qty and is Sold; a manager PATCHes status Sold->Done: no committed claim exists, so the sold units become sellable again and can be sold twice. (b) A line In Transit under a Pending transfer is PATCHed to Done: receive skips it (inventory.ts:~2002) and discard refuses it (inventory.ts:~2168), so the transfer is stuck. (c) Setting a line to Draft leaves Draft/Packing SOs naming it unpromotable.
findings.proposed_fix: Share cascadeBlockers' rules with the inventory editor: refuse leaving Sold, refuse status changes on lines whose transfer_order_id is a Pending transfer, and when the new status is not sellable also check open draft/packing claims (or require a confirm).
findings.regression_test: Sell a lot out to Done, PATCH /api/inventory/:id {status:'Done'} -> 409; PATCH an In Transit line under a Pending transfer -> 409.

findings.title: Deleting a transfer's source warehouse (no transferTo) makes discard of that transfer fail with an FK 500 forever
findings.evidence: Delete only blocks on to_warehouse_id; it sets transfer_orders.from_warehouse_id = NULL (transferTo is null). Discard computes origin = ord.from_warehouse_id ?? detail.from, and detail.from in the append-only 'transferred' inventory_event still names the deleted warehouse. Mixed-source transfers (from_warehouse_id NULL) hit it even with transferTo. The delete also rewrites order_lines.warehouse_id without inventory_events.
findings.failure_scenario: TO-1 Pending WH-A->WH-B; manager deletes WH-A without transferTo; discard TO-1 runs UPDATE order_lines SET warehouse_id='WH-A' -> FK violation -> 500; TO-1 can never be discarded and its lines stay In Transit.
findings.proposed_fix: Refuse warehouse delete while Pending transfers have lines whose transferred events name it, or have discard verify the origin exists and fall back to NULL / transferTo; write a warehouse_reassigned inventory_event per moved line.
findings.regression_test: Create pending transfer from WH-A, DELETE /api/warehouses/WH-A, POST discard -> 200 (or 409 on the delete), never 500.

findings.title: Archive's removeFromSellOrders is a bare boolean; the removal set is recomputed after the manager confirms
findings.evidence: The 409 lists the claimed SO lines; the retry sends only removeFromSellOrders:true and archiveOrderLinesTx deletes whatever 'claimed' finds now (openSellStatuses includes committed statuses). Also the SO pre-lock at :374-381 uses an EXISTS subquery evaluated on the statement snapshot, so an SO that gains a claim while the line lock (cascadeBlockers) waits is first locked by the UPDATE sell_orders at :422 — lines before SO header, against the documented order in orderLocks.ts.
findings.failure_scenario: Manager A archives PO-1, sees a 409 naming SO-1 (Draft). Manager B adds a PO-1 line to SO-2 and ships it. A confirms: the archive silently deletes the line from Shipped SO-2 and clears its negotiated total, which A never saw. Under the concurrent variant, a save on SO-2 racing the archive can deadlock (40P01 -> 500).
findings.proposed_fix: Have the client echo the confirmed sol_id set and return a fresh 409 if claimed differs; lock the SOs named by claimed before the line lock (re-read until stable).
findings.regression_test: Archive -> 409 listing SO-1; add line to SO-2 and ship; retry with removeFromSellOrders -> expect 409 listing SO-2, SO-2 unchanged.

findings.title: Transfer receive/reopen/discard lock lines with no ORDER BY
findings.evidence: FOR UPDATE OF l without ORDER BY, while the PO cascade and delete lock a PO's lines ORDER BY id; discard locks peers after clones.
findings.failure_scenario: A transfer holding two lines of one PO is received while that PO advances stage: heap-order vs id-order locking can deadlock (40P01 surfaced as 500).
findings.proposed_fix: Add ORDER BY l.id to the locking SELECTs; lock clones and peers together in sorted order.

findings.title: Reopen + discard of a transfer can delete a clone lot a Draft sell order names
findings.evidence: Reopen and discard only count committed claims; discard's sell-order guard is on the peer, not the clone it deletes. sell_order_lines.inventory_id is ON DELETE SET NULL (migration 0127).
findings.failure_scenario: Partial transfer creates clone C, received, C added to Draft SO-1, transfer reopened (no committed claim) and discarded: C merges back and is deleted; SO-1's line silently loses its source.
findings.proposed_fix: Give reopen the proposal/confirmDrafts check transfer create uses; in discard refuse (or skip merge) when an open SO names the clone.
findings.regression_test: The scenario above returns 409 or keeps C referenced.

findings.title: PATCH can blank required names (remaining half of BD-08); supplier PATCH 500s on duplicate match_key and bad nextFollowUpAt/cadenceDays
findings.evidence: COALESCE('', name) stores empty string; suppliers PATCH writes name untrimmed (null -> NOT NULL 500) and has no catch for suppliers_owner_match_idx unlike POST/adopt; nextFollowUpAt/cadenceDays unvalidated.
findings.failure_scenario: PATCH customer {name:''} -> 200 blank customer; rename client B to client A's name in same book -> 500 instead of 409; nextFollowUpAt:'x' -> 22007 500.
findings.proposed_fix: Require nonblank trimmed name/label in PATCH validators; map unique violation to 409; validate date and integer cadence.

findings.title: Sell-order unitPrice has no upper bound or scale check: numeric overflow is a 500
findings.evidence: lineInputError checks only finite and >= 0; unit_price/source_unit_price are NUMERIC(12,2). RMB prices with 3+ decimals are stored rounded while USD is converted from the unrounded value (sellOrders.ts:~911, sellOrderCreate.ts:~191).
findings.failure_scenario: POST /api/sell-orders with unitPrice 1e10 -> SQLSTATE 22003 inside the txn -> 500.
findings.proposed_fix: Cap unitPrice (like afterSales MAX_AMOUNT) and reject >2 decimals before conversion.

findings.title: After-sales summary silently drops RMB cases when no USD/CNY rate exists, and uses a different rate than accounting
findings.evidence: cnyPerUsdOnFrag returns NULL with empty fx_rates; amount/NULL is NULL and SUM skips it while COUNT(*) counts it. Summary converts at the case-open-day rate, accounting target at the latest rate.
findings.failure_scenario: Fresh dev/test DB, one RMB case of 700: tile shows {count:1, amount:0}. In prod the same case shows two different USD figures on the after-sales tiles and the accounting page.
findings.proposed_fix: Return an unconverted count (or fall back to latest rate) and pick one conversion rule for both screens.
findings.regression_test: Summary with an RMB case and empty fx_rates does not report a silent 0.

findings.title: RS-483 did not update docs/DATABASE.md for after_sales_cases.currency_code
findings.evidence: The after_sales_cases section has no currency_code row or CHECK and still describes amount as USD; apps/backend/AGENTS.md requires the doc change in the same PR.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of DATABASE.md sums after_sales_cases.amount as USD and mixes RMB refunds into USD totals.
findings.proposed_fix: Add currency_code char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USD', CHECK IN ('USD','CNY'), 'amount is in currency_code'.

findings.title: Duplicate-lot sell-order diff pairs occurrences by position, mislabelling removals as edits (residual of BD-07)
findings.evidence: Within a lot bucket the n-th before occurrence is paired with the n-th after occurrence in position order.
findings.failure_scenario: Lot X at pos0 {2,New} and pos1 {3,Used}; manager deletes pos0. Timeline records line_edited X 2->3 New->Used plus line_removed {3,Used} instead of removed {2,New}; a pure reorder writes two phantom line_edited events.
findings.proposed_fix: Cancel identical snapshots first (tupleKey multiset), then pair the remainder by fewest changed fields.
findings.regression_test: diffSellOrderLines([X/2/New,X/3/Used],[X/3/Used]) -> removed=[X/2/New], edited=[]; swapped order -> empty diff.

findings.title: Sub-cent PO values revert a submitted PO to Draft for an edit that never lands
findings.evidence: changesMaterialField compares numbers at 1e-9 while columns are NUMERIC(12,2) and validateLineInput does not limit decimals.
findings.failure_scenario: Purchaser saves a Reviewing PO with unitCost 33.333 (stored 33.33): PO reverts to Draft, managers notified, stored value unchanged and a 'reverted' event with empty changes is written.
findings.proposed_fix: Round money inputs to 2 dp before comparing; only write reverted when something changed.
findings.regression_test: PATCH Reviewing PO with stored+0.003 -> lifecycle stays reviewing, no reverted event.

findings.title: Draft PO delete reads sell-order claims without locking the lines
findings.evidence: Delete checks sell_order_lines unlocked, then deletes the order; SO create locks only the lines.
findings.failure_scenario: A Draft PO line hand-set to Done is claimed by a SO committing between the check and the DELETE; cascade sets sell_order_lines.inventory_id NULL, orphaning the SO line.
findings.proposed_fix: Lock the PO's lines ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE before the claim check.
findings.regression_test: Two-connection interleave -> 409 or clean, never NULL inventory_id.

findings.title: Package subqueries inside locking SELECTs read a pre-wait snapshot
findings.evidence: has_package / pkg subqueries are evaluated with the statement snapshot taken before the FOR NO KEY UPDATE wait (same class as BD-02).
findings.failure_scenario: PATCH adding a tracking number commits while /advance enforce:'all' waits on the PO lock: advance wrongly refuses missingTracking.
findings.proposed_fix: Read packages in a separate statement after the lock.
findings.regression_test: Barrier test: advance waits on PATCH inserting a package, then succeeds.

findings.title: 'submitted' order event records raw line sum, ignoring a negotiated lot price
findings.evidence: Computes SUM(qty*unit_cost) rather than the goods total syncOrderGoodsTotal maintains (pinned orders.total_cost, qty_purchased).
findings.failure_scenario: PO with agreed $8,500 lot price over lines summing $9,000 shows 'submitted at $9,000' in the audit timeline.
findings.regression_test: Submit a pinned-total PO and assert detail.totalCost.

findings.title: GET /api/inventory/:id leaks transfer_order_id to purchasers
findings.evidence: Selects l.* and the purchaser branch strips only cost fields, while event reads strip transfer ids because transfer orders are manager-only (:42-48).
findings.failure_scenario: A purchaser GETs a transferred line of their own PO and sees the manager-only transfer order id.
findings.proposed_fix: delete r.transfer_order_id in the purchaser branch.

findings.title: [carryover BD-11] services/orderAdvance.ts and routes/sellOrders.ts import packing persistence from a route module
findings.evidence: import { prunePackRows } from '../routes/sellOrderPack' — service depends on HTTP registration (route->service->route cycle).
findings.failure_scenario: Structural: a change to sellOrderPack.ts route registration or its imports affects the archive lifecycle path; blocks an import-boundary check.
findings.proposed_fix: Move keyedLines/prunePackRows into services/sellOrderPack.ts; add an import-boundary lint.
findings.regression_test: Existing sell-order-pack / orders-archive tests stay green; boundary check passes.

Source files were read in full (split across three reviewer passes, every P2 re-verified against the code by the lane owner). lib/sellOrderPriceTemplate.ts was only scanned (the shell treats it as binary; export-only). The ~150 test files in A2.files.txt were not reviewed one by one: only tier1-data-integrity.test.ts (BD-10) was read, and stock-lock-order/review-lock-protocol were checked for existence. No tests were run, because the backend baseline had not finished (no DONE in baseline/summary.txt) and no repro tests were written. Money: stored amounts are numeric(12,2) and the ::float use is display/export only, so no integer-cents defect was found beyond A2-07/A2-11. RS-483: the currency enum matches the DB CHECK, POST/PATCH validation agree, audit events carry currency, and old rows default to USD. No live resources touched.
